title: Fix weighted Kaplan-Meier rounding and Cox baseline strata labels
description:
With non-integer case weights, the Kaplan-Meier estimate could end at a tiny residue instead of exactly 0, sometimes negative (about -9e-17), with an infinite standard error and an overflow warning. A survivor weight that is zero up to rounding is now treated as zero.

`CoxPH.baseline_hazard()` now follows the result-structure rule in `spec/results.md`: a `strata` column comes first, labeled `"all"` or `"sex=1"`, while `predict(strata=)` still takes the raw values. Polars Series passed alongside `data=` now keep their name in curve labels.

title: feat: enhanced data ingest
description:
This PR reworks data ingest so the same code runs on Pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, and lazy frames. Responses, covariates, and grouping columns are named instead of extracted (`gw.Surv.right(time="time", event="status", data=lung, event_value=2)`), and event codings are declared as values rather than written as data frame expressions.

A new `Outcome` describes an endpoint once and is bound to data at fit time, dropping incomplete rows once across the response, covariates, and labels, with R's "observations deleted due to missingness" note. R users can pass a whole formula (`"Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex + strata(inst)"`), including `duration()`, `cluster()`, and `frailty()` terms. `Surv.first_event()` builds competing-risks responses from per-endpoint column pairs.

Also, models now keep their covariate design, so `predict()` accepts any frame holding the fitted columns and codes categories with the fitted levels. The docs use the new API throughout.

title: fix: keep stratified cross-validation folds balanced
description:
# Summary

The stratified splitter assigns every stratum's remainder to the first folds. Six rows split into five folds can therefore produce sizes [2, 2, 2, 0, 0]. Empty folds also become float indices, causing cross-validation to fail.

Rotate the starting fold between strata, preserve integer indices, and reject k above the retained complete-case row count. Update the docstring and user guide.

# Validation

- Nine of eleven new cases fail before the fix; two controls already pass.
- Resampling, Outcome, and penalized-model suites: 181 passed.
- Full Python suite: 2,373 passed, 16 skipped, 5 warnings.
- Ruff lint/format and Pyright passed.

Corrected fold assignments can change fixed-seed scores and cv_coxnet penalty selection. Same-seed reproducibility is preserved.

# Checklist

- [x] Python checks passed.
- [x] Regression tests added.
- [x] Docstring and user guide updated.

Estimator and scoring formulas are unchanged; no R-parity fixtures were modified.

title: fix: evaluate duplicate cross-validation metrics once
description:
# Summary

Repeated metric names in cross_validate() currently duplicate fold scores and distort the reported standard deviation. Three folds with metrics=["concordance", "concordance"] return six scores.

Evaluate each metric once, preserving first-occurrence order and leaving the caller's list unchanged. Update the docstring and user guide.

# Validation

- Both new regression cases fail before the fix.
- Resampling and Outcome suites: 99 passed.
- Full Python suite: 2,364 passed, 16 skipped, 5 warnings.
- Ruff lint/format and Pyright passed.

# Checklist

- [x] Python checks passed.
- [x] Regression tests added.
- [x] Docstring and user guide updated.

Estimator and scoring formulas are unchanged; no R-parity fixtures were modified.

title: fix: preserve unobserved causes in accuracy_in_time
description:
# Summary

`accuracy_in_time()` counts only observed event causes when validating prediction arrays, although the cause axis must follow the response's declared states. With states `("relapse", "death")` and only death events (code 2), it rejects valid two-cause predictions. A compressed one-cause array is instead accepted and can return an incorrect accuracy.

Use `Surv.states` when available to preserve cause codes across subsets, retain the existing single-event fallback, and clarify the docstring. Add five regression cases for missing first/middle/last causes, all-censored data, and rejection of compressed cause axes.

# Validation

- All five new cases fail on the original implementation.
- Metrics and Outcome suites: 146 passed.
- Full Python suite: 2,367 passed, 16 skipped, 5 warnings.
- Ruff lint/format and Pyright passed.

The full suite ran with two workers and coverage from `python/`. Existing skips include optional great-tables visualizations and dependency-specific forest paths. No estimator formulas or R-generated fixtures changed.

# Checklist

- [x] Python checks passed: Ruff, Pyright, and pytest.
- [x] Regression tests added.
- [x] Docstring updated.

R-parity fixture changes are not applicable: this fixes cause-axis validation without changing estimator formulas.

title: Fix/terminal visit event
description:
# Summary

Thank you for contributing to Greenwood! Please explain the context and purpose of your
contribution, and list the changes made to the code or docs.

# Related GitHub Issues and PRs

- Ref: #

# Checklist

- [x] `make check` passes (ruff, pyright, pytest).
- [x] I have added tests for any new functionality.
- [x] For new/changed statistics, I have added or updated R-parity fixtures.
- [x] I have updated docs (docstrings and/or `user_guide/`) as needed.

title: Set up the R + Python monorepo and a minimal R package
description: This reorganizes the repo so Python and R implementations of Greenwood can live side by side.

title: feat: MPS
description: This PR adds a three-parameter (threshold/location) extension to `AFT` for Weibull, exponential, log-normal, and log-logistic models (`AFT(threshold=True)`, not supported for `gengamma`), together with a new `method="mps"` estimation option (maximum product of spacings.

title: feat: Turnbull estimator
description: This PR adds Turnbull, a self-consistent NPMLE estimator for interval-censored survival data, filling the gap left by `KaplanMeier`/`NelsonAalen`, which require exact-or-right-censored event times. It accepts `Surv.interval()` (the general case) as well as `Surv.right()`/`Surv.left()`, computes the data's maximal intersection intervals via the Gentleman & Geyer construction, and solves for their probabilities via EM self-consistency. Where the data leave a region genuinely unidentified, `predict()`/`quantile()`/`median()` report both interval bounds and return `nan` rather than interpolate a false point estimate.

title: feat: AFT residuals
description: This PR adds a `residuals()` method to the AFT class (supporting several residual types). This brings AFT diagnostic capabilities on par with CoxPH. The User Guide documents each residual type with worked examples, and the glossary adds entries for Cox-Snell and response residuals.

title: feat: Weibull plots
description:
This PR adds `plot_weibull()`, which is a diagnostic visualization that plots Kaplan-Meier survival estimates on transformed axes (where a specified parametric distribution appears as a straight line). Supports three distribution transforms (these are: Weibull cloglog, log-normal probit, log-logistic logit), stratified KM for visual PH assumption checking, and an optional fitted AFT parametric overlay for unstratified fits.

Fixes: https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/issues/22

title: feat: Mixture Cure models
description: This PR adds support for the Mixture Cure model to the package, including its integration into the public API, dataset management, R-parity fixtures, and a few unit tests.

title: feat: additive hazards cure models
description: This PR adds support for the Aalen additive hazards model. The main changes include implementing the `AalenAdditive` estimator, integrating it into the package API, and providing R-parity test fixtures for validation against R's `survival::aareg`. This addition allows users to fit additive hazards models with time-varying coefficients, providing an alternative to Cox regression when the proportional hazards assumption does not hold.

title: feat: IPCRidge
description: This PR introduces support for Inverse Probability of Censoring Weighting (IPCW) and IPC-weighted ridge regression to the codebase. It adds new classes for estimating the censoring distribution and fitting penalized regression models that account for censoring.

title: feat: add ML models
description: This PR introduces a new machine learning module for tree-based survival analysis. The big highlights are the addition of tree-based ensemble survival models (including gradient boosting), new plotting functions for per-subject survival predictions, and solid test coverage for these new features.

title: feat: IPCW concordance index
description: This PR adds support for the inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted (IPCW) concordance index (Uno's C), making discrimination assessment more robust under heavy or non-uniform censoring. It introduces the new `concordance_index_ipcw()` function, documents its use, adds R-parity fixtures and tests, and updates the User Guide with usage examples and guidance.

title: feat: Gray's test for comparing CIFs
description: This PR adds support for Gray's test. Here, it's a single function that tests whether cumulative incidence functions differ across groups in the presence of competing risks. It aligns with the existing AalenJohansen and FineGray infrastructure, and it's the competing-risks analogue of the log-rank test.

title: feat: generalized gamma regression
description: This PR introduces support for the generalized gamma accelerated failure time (AFT) model, enhancing the package's parametric modeling capabilities.

title: feat: flexible parametric models
description: This PR introduces support for piecewise exponential models (PEM), including a new `PiecewiseExponential` class, several unit tests, and user guide documentation.

title: feat: smooth HR curves
description: This PR introduces a new feature for visualizing and diagnosing non-linear effects of continuous covariates in Cox proportional hazards models: smooth hazard ratio (HR) curves. It adds a `smooth_hr()` method to `CoxPH`, a `SmoothHRResult` data structure, and a `plot_smooth_hr()` plotting function with both Altair and plotnine backends.

title: feat: time stratified PH tests
description: This PR adds support for windowed (time-stratified) proportional-hazards tests in the Cox model, allowing users to assess the proportional-hazards assumption within specific time intervals. This is achieved by introducing a new `breaks=` argument to `CoxPH.cox_zph()`, which splits the follow-up period into user-defined windows and computes Grambsch-Therneau test statistics for each window. The results are accessible via the new `ZPHWindowResult` class and are integrated into the `ZPHResult` output and its DataFrame export methods.

title: perf: optimization
description: Replaced O(K*n) per-event-time boolean scans with O(1) lookups via reverse cumulative sums in five areas of the codebase. Results in 20x-40x speedups for CoxPH.fit(), cox_zph(), and various internal functions.

title: feat: viz outliers
description: This PR introduces a new diagnostic visualization function for Cox proportional hazards models, `plot_influence()`, which provides scatter-plot panels for identifying influential and outlying observations. The function supports both Altair and plotnine backends.

title: feat: leverage hat-matrix diagnostics
description: This PR adds support for leverage (hat-matrix diagonal) diagnostics to the Cox proportional hazards model implementation and introduces a new method for comprehensive influence diagnostics.

title: feat: predictive intervals
description: This PR introduces robust support for confidence intervals (CIs) in Cox proportional hazards model predictions, specifically adding CI support for conditional survival probabilities (with `conditional_after`) and for time-varying covariate trajectories. It also adds thorough tests for these features, aligns the Python implementation with R's `survfit` for conditional CIs, and removes outdated documentation about unsupported CI options.

title: feat: bootstrap CIs
description: This PR introduces robust bootstrap resampling and confidence interval support, along with documentation updates and tests. It also updates cross-validation and performance assessment features to better reflect the new capabilities.

title: feat: clustered robust variance for Kaplan-Meier
description: This PR adds support for clustered robust variance estimation to the Kaplan-Meier estimator. This allows users to account for within-cluster correlation (e.g., patients nested in groups) when estimating survival curves and their standard errors. The implementation introduces a new `cluster=` argument to the `fit()` method and updates the internal variance calculations.

title: feat: sandwich variance for KM
description: This PR adds robust (sandwich/infinitesimal-jackknife) variance estimation for Kaplan-Meier estimators, matching R's `survfit(..., robust=TRUE)`. The implementation allows users to compute correct confidence intervals and standard errors for survival curves when using non-integer weights or clustered/correlated data. The main changes are the addition of the robust variance option, updates to the API and documentation, and new test fixtures for robust variance.

title: Feat: AIC and BIC support for CoxNet
description: This PR provides support for model selection using information criteria (AIC and BIC) for penalized Cox regression models (`CoxNet`). It introduces methods to compute the effective degrees of freedom for penalized fits, and, implements AIC/BIC calculations.

title: feat: time transformations for `cox_zph`
description: This PR adds support for two additional time transformations (Kaplan-Meier (`"km"`) and rank-based (`"rank"`)) to the `cox_zph` proportional hazards test for Cox models. It updates the implementation, documentation, test fixtures, and user guide to reflect these new options. We also ensure compatibility with R's `cox.zph()` function.

title: feat: multi-metric CV
description: This PR adds multi-metric cross-validation support to the `cross_validate()` function. This allows for evaluating several metrics (concordance, Brier score, and time-dependent AUC) in a single run. It also adds support for the `RoystonParmar` model in cross-validation.

title: feat: expected RMST predictions
description: This PR adds support for expected (restricted mean) survival time (RMST) predictions to all major survival models in the codebase, including Cox proportional hazards, parametric AFT, and Royston-Parmar flexible models. The new `predict_expectation()` method provides RMST estimates up to a user-specified time horizon (`tau`), with optional confidence intervals, and outputs results in a consistent DataFrame format.

title: feat: add support for time-varying covariates
description: This PR adds support for time-varying covariates in Cox regression models by introducing the `split_episodes` utility and extending the `CoxPH.predict()` method to handle covariate trajectories. It also adds the `pbcseq` dataset for repeated lab measurements, updates documentation (with a new User Guide page), and makes related API and docstring improvements.

title: feat: stratified survival predictions
description: This PR adds support for survival prediction in stratified Cox models, allowing users to obtain survival probabilities for each subject using the correct stratum-specific baseline hazard. It introduces a new `strata=` argument to the `predict()` method, updates the documentation and user guide, and adds tests for the new functionality.

title: feat: lognormal shared frailty
description: This PR implements `frailty="lognormal"` in `CoxPH.fit()`. It's the follow-on PR to the existing gamma frailty. The log-normal model places a random effect on the log-hazard for each cluster (this is more flexible than gamma for hazard heterogeneity).

title: feat: Cox residual diagnostics
description: This PR adds support for Cox model residual diagnostics, expanding the available residual types and harmonizing their computation and documentation. It also introduces new test fixtures for validating these diagnostics against R's `survival` package.

title: ci: AFT survival prediction CI tests
description: This PR adds several new tests for CI support in AFT survival predictions. The new tests verify CI column structure, bracket correctness, and value bounds for survival predictions across multiple distributions (`weibull`, `exponential`, `lognormal`, `loglogistic`). We also add some testing for CI behavior with different confidence levels (i.e., wider intervals at higher confidence).

title: fix: Cox baseline hazard CI
description: This PR improves the calculation and testing of baseline hazard CIs in the Cox proportional hazards implementation. It now ensures that results match R's `survfit.coxph`. There's a correction to the log-log CI standard error calculation and a new R fixture generation along with parity tests.

title: docs: docstring improvements
description: This focus of this PR is to improve the clarity, completeness, and consistency of the documentation throughout the docstrings of exported objects. The changes include expanded explanations of function parameters and return values, improved usage examples, and clarifications on model interpretation and output formats. Additionally, several docstrings have been refactored for readability, and some sections now provide more detailed info on stats concepts and diagnostics.

title: feat: add initial support for frailty models
description: This PR adds support for shared gamma frailty models to the `CoxPH` class, enabling random cluster-level effects for correlated survival data (e.g., repeated events, multi-center, or familial studies). The implementation includes frailty variance estimation, likelihood-ratio testing, and exposes relevant parameters and results.

title: feat: cross-validated penalizer selection for CoxNet (`cv_coxnet()`)
description: This PR adds `cv_coxnet()` and `CoxNetCVResult` for automatic lambda selection in elastic-net Cox models. It can: (1) search a log-spaced path anchored at lambda max (derived from the score at beta=0), (2) score each value by stratified k-fold CV (concordance or integrated Brier), and (3) return the best penalizer plus the 1-SE rule alternative.

title: feat: add stratified k-fold cross-validation (to ensure balanced event representation across folds)
description: This PR introduces important improvements to numerical stability checks and user guidance in the Cox proportional hazards model and CV routines. There's now automatic detection and warnings for poorly scaled covariates and low event rates during cross-validation. The User Guide (two separate guide pages) has new material for helping users interpret and resolve these issues.

title: Feat: Add CIF CI `conf_type=` parameter
description: This PR adds the `conf_type=` parameter to `AalenJohansen` for CIF confidence intervals. The `AalenJohansen` estimator previously only produced plain (Wald) confidence intervals for the cumulative incidence function. The `conf_type=` parameter supports three transforms (`"plain"` (default), `"log"`, and `"log-log"`) matching the CI options already available on `KaplanMeier`.

title: feat: exploratory CIF plots
description:
This PR refactors the visualization API for cumulative incidence function (CIF) and survival plots to improve clarity and consistency. We standardize plot naming to `plot_*()` and implement grouped CIF visualization.

We also implement the following here:

- `plot_cif(aj)` accepts a fitted `AalenJohansen` directly, renders step functions faceted by competing cause, colored by group when stratified via `by=` (with a shaded confidence band)
- `risk_table=True` draws an aligned numbers-at-risk table beneath the panels, with optional custom `times=`

title: feat: add univariate parametric models
description: This PR adds support for univariate parametric survival models. The big addition is the new `Parametric` class (for fitting and predicting with parametric survival distributions). We also add a `compare_distributions()` utility for model selection.

title: feat: time dependent AUC
description: This PR adds time-dependent AUC metrics for survival analysis, implementing the IPCW (Inverse Probability of Censoring Weighting) estimator by Uno. This adds the `time_dependent_auc()` and `integrated_auc()` functions to the metrics API.

title: feat: enhancements to AFT predictions
description: This PR adds new prediction capabilities to the parametric AFT model. It enables direct computation of mean survival time, conditional mean, expected remaining lifetime, and restricted mean survival time (RMST) for all supported distributions. The changes include closed-form and numerically robust formulas, expanded documentation, and improved error handling for these new prediction types.

title: feat: forest plots for Cox HRs
description: This PR consolidates and modernizes the forest plot API. It replaces the previous `forest_plot()` function with the modernized `plot_forest()` function. The changes update all relevant imports, public API exports, documentation, and tests to use the new interface, and provide expanded test coverage for the new functionality.

title: feat: stratified RMST comparison
description: This PR adds support for stratified RMST (Restricted Mean Survival Time) comparisons, allowing users to control for confounding variables when comparing two groups. The implementation follows the standard inverse-variance pooling approach (and this matches implementations in R's `survRM2` and `survival` packages).

title: feat: add CI for baseline hazard and survival predictions in both the CoxPH and parametric AFT models
description: This PR adds support for confidence intervals for baseline hazard and survival predictions in both the Cox proportional hazards and parametric AFT models. It adds options to compute and return confidence bounds using either a log-log transform or plain Wald intervals, improving interpretability and parity with R's `survfit()`.

title: feat: add stratified CV
description: This PR introduces several new visualization functions and improves the API for plotting survival curves. Also, we add here stratified k-fold cross-validation for survival data.

title: fix: CoxPH coefficients not invariant to uniform weight scaling
description: This PR introduces an important fix for the Cox proportional hazards model implementation. It ensures that model coefficients and predictions are invariant to uniform scaling of sample weights. This is achieved by normalizing the weights internally and improving numerical stability in the computation. There are many new tests added here to make sure that the fix is solid (and to prevent future regressions).

title: Bring the R package to near parity with Python
description: This PR adds native R versions of most of the Python estimators, tests, and metrics. As before, survival is in Suggests for validation only and is not used at runtime. Every table starts with a `strata` column, which is `"all"` when there is only one curve.
